recent_posts.title: A Software Engineer’s Guide to Observability: Part 1 - Logging
recent_posts.summary: A comprehensive guide to implementing effective logging practices in distributed systems. Covers the fundamentals of why logs serve as forensic tools, what events and data attributes to capture, how to structure logs using JSON format with correlation IDs, and best practices for consistent logging across services. Emphasizes preparing logs for AI consumption while avoiding common pitfalls like logging sensitive data or creating excessive noise.

recent_posts.title: A Software Engineer’s Guide to Observability
recent_posts.summary: A comprehensive guide to observability for engineering teams, covering the three pillars (logging, tracing, metrics) and their practical applications. Explains why observability has become critical in the era of distributed systems and AI-generated code, where complexity is increasing while domain expertise is becoming more distributed. The guide focuses on understanding when and why to use different observability tools rather than just how to configure them.

recent_posts.title: 🔐 AccessOrbit: One-Click, Time-Limited DB Access with Hashicorp Vault & GitHub Actions
recent_posts.summary: AccessOrbit at Blueground offers a secure, auditable, and automated process for engineers to access databases using HashiCorp Vault for ephemeral credentials and GitHub Actions for request automation. It involves creating a database secrets engine, defining connection roles, and utilizing Slack for notifications and approvals. The solution ensures least privilege access and auto-expiration of credentials, reducing security risks and manual workflow chaos.

recent_posts.title: Building an AI-powered team knowledge base with ease
recent_posts.summary: Building an AI-powered knowledge base in-house is feasible and cost-effective using tools like Cloudflare's AutoRAG and Next.js. This approach allows customization to meet team-specific needs, offers detailed integration of various data sources, and ensures a visually appealing user interface. The architecture is scalable, secure, and designed for future enhancements, setting new standards for knowledge management in the age of AI.

recent_posts.title: 98% Faster Data Imports in Deployment Previews
recent_posts.summary: Engineers faced delays in previewing pull requests due to lengthy data import times in ephemeral environments. By utilizing Velero and Kubernetes PVC snapshotting, a significant bottleneck was resolved. The optimized process reduced data import times from 19 minutes to just 25 seconds, enhancing productivity and developer experience. Persistent Volumes (PVs) and Persistent Volume Claims (PVCs) play a critical role in this setup.

recent_posts.title: Mastering UI Testing for Android web forms
recent_posts.summary: Integrating web-based functionality into Android apps can present challenges, particularly during UI testing. This post explores an issue where a button in a web form remains disabled despite valid inputs being provided programmatically. The root cause is the 'non-trusted' nature of JavaScript events in such scenarios. To overcome this, the post suggests simulating real user input through the keyboard using Espresso's Instrumentation class, ensuring the web form behaves as expected during tests.

recent_posts.title: Accelerating theblueground.com: Five Core Web Vitals improvements
recent_posts.summary: Blueground, a provider of fully furnished apartments, focuses on optimizing their website for Google's Core Web Vitals to ensure fast, seamless user interactions. They tackled challenges like Largest Contentful Paint (LCP) and implemented various performance enhancements, such as geographic server distribution, cross-region database replication, critical CSS extraction, font preloading, and image optimization. These efforts have resulted in a 50% acceleration in Time to First Byte (TTFB) and a significant reduction in First Contentful Paint (FCP) and LCP scores on mobile devices. They continue to explore further optimizations for even better performance.

recent_posts.title: Crafting a Floating Bubble in Android with Jetpack Compose
recent_posts.summary: Jetpack Compose facilitates the creation of a draggable floating bubble UI in Android apps. This implementation defines draggable areas using composable components and leverages state tracking to manage the bubble's position and size. By using modifiers such as onGloballyPositioned and pointerInput, the bubble can be accurately positioned and restricted to stay within the app's bounds. This method ensures a seamless and intuitive user experience.

recent_posts.title: Fixtures made easy with KSP
recent_posts.summary: Blueground has developed an open-source tool called Fixtures, inspired by Philipp Hauer's blog post, to automate the generation of helper functions for data class instantiation in tests. By using the @Fixture annotation, helper functions are automatically generated, reducing boilerplate code. The tool also supports random data generation, handling unsupported field types with @FixtureAdapter, and overcoming issues related to source sets and multi-module projects.

recent_posts.title: A different way to run the daily scrum
recent_posts.summary: Daily scrums can sometimes feel unproductive and tiresome. An alternative format called the 'per-PBI' approach focuses on each PBI (Product Backlog Item) rather than each person. This method encourages collaboration, planning, and reduces lead times by prioritizing moving PBIs to completion. While this format can increase the duration of daily scrums, it fosters better team cohesion and more effective planning.
